speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To start, can you tell me when these symptoms of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and arm weakness first began? Also, have you noticed if the double vision changes depending on which direction you look?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking, especially towards the end of the day? Also, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking, especially towards the end of the day? Have you also noticed any drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you haven't mentioned your eyelids yet; do you experience any drooping, particularly later in the day? Additionally, does your double vision improve after you take a short rest?

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any drooping of your eyelids, especially later in the day or after looking upward? Given the fluctuating weakness and eye symptoms, I would like to order a specific test to help confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Titers

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated). Additional findings include ptosis of the right upper eyelid worsening with sustained upward gaze, diminished motor strength in upper extremities with normal tone, and electromyography showing decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation. Chest CT is normal with no thymoma detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated antibodies, worsening eyelid droop, and characteristic EMG findings confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
